keywords.help: How far, in pixels, a hole's fill searches outward for a measured value to interpolate from.
keywords.source: GDAL gdal_fillnodata -md: "The maximum distance (in pixels) that the algorithm will search out for values to interpolate. The default is 100 pixels." https://gdal.org/en/stable/programs/gdal_fillnodata.html

keywords.help: The interpolator a hole is filled with: GDAL's inverse-distance weighting, the library's own.
keywords.source: GDAL FillNodata (rasterio.fill.fillnodata), the library's native algorithm; the only one the fill implements. https://gdal.org/en/stable/programs/gdal_fillnodata.html

keywords.help: Cells between two merged datasets interpolated so the bed levels pass smoothly from one to the other; 0 leaves the seam as measured.
keywords.source: HydroMT-SFINCS merge_multi_dataarrays buffer_cells: "Number of cells between datasets to ensure smooth transition of bed levels, by default 0" https://github.com/Deltares/hydromt_sfincs/blob/main/hydromt_sfincs/workflows/merge.py

keywords.help: The most cells one merge builds over the union of its inputs; a merge past it refuses by name rather than coarsening the measurement.
How each merged input is resampled onto the common grid.
keywords.source: TRID3NT engineering default. HydroMT-SFINCS picks bilinear when the next dataset is as coarse as or coarser than the first and average when finer.

keywords.help: How many times the last input's relief two merged populations may stand apart before the merge refuses them as a cliff.
The most cells a coverage read builds over a cut; a finer raster is read on a coarser grid for the count, never for its values.
The most DEM cells the D8 flow-direction chain takes before it refuses; cost grows with the grid (about 40 s at 4000 x 4000).
The most eHydro channel surveys one read lays over an area before it stops adding more.
The share of the area a further eHydro survey must newly cover to be taken.
How far past a mesh's extent, as a fraction of its own span, the bed is fetched so its rim is read, not filled.
How a bed raster is read between cell centres at a mesh's nodes: nearest returns a value the grid holds, bilinear interpolates.
The share of a node's bilinear footprint that must be measured for the node to take a value; below it the node is a hole.
The QGIS algorithm a refusal names for gridding soundings into a bed surface.
How many cadences a gap between two rain stamps spans before it counts as a missing report.
The default bound, in native intervals, on a hole a series bridges: within-cadence interpolation is refinement, bridging three missed reports is invention.
How far back of a run's moment a sample still speaks for the water it was taken from.
How close, in metres, a pixel must sit to a water body's modal elevation to count as its hydro-flattened surface.
keywords.source: USGS Elevation-Derived Hydrography Data Acquisition Specifications, Vertical Alignment of lake/pond polygons: a water body's z-values match its hydro-flattened surface within 0.001 m.

keywords.help: How long a gate card waits for a reply before it expires as a typed timeout, never a silent proceed.
How many times a review card is redrawn on a person's picks before the run is refused unlaunched.
The wall clock a request run in the user's QGIS session may take before the call resolves as a timeout.
How long a tool-candidates card waits for a pick before the turn falls back to autonomous routing.
